headline: Delhivery reports Q2 revenue above ₹3,000 crore as EBITDA nearly triples
summary: Logistics firm Delhivery posted its Q2 results with quarterly revenue crossing ₹3,000 crore for the first time in company history. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) nearly tripled year-on-year. The sharp jump reflects improving operational scale and cost efficiencies across its express parcel and network logistics operations. The performance offers a positive signal for retail shareholders tracking profitability in India's logistics technology sector.
why_it_matters: Stronger operational margins bolster investor confidence in new-age tech logistics.

headline: Delhivery submits quarterly compliance certificate to SEBI

It is a standard procedural requirement for all listed companies in India. The filing ensures the company remains in compliance with stock exchange listing obligations.

headline: How high product return rates are squeezing profit margins for Indian e-commerce sellers
hook: The hidden cost of online returns
summary: Product returns in Indian e-commerce, often reaching 20% to 30% of total orders, are severely impacting the profitability of online sellers. Reverse logistics, repackaging, and transit damages significantly inflate operational expenses for digital merchants. While logistics providers like Delhivery earn revenue on both delivery and return legs, e-commerce platforms face compressed margins. This operational leak directly depresses the earnings of listed consumer-tech companies.
why_it_matters: High return rates squeeze margins of listed e-commerce firms
winners_losers: Logistics firms gain / E-commerce sellers hurt
